definition: Control processes are the cognitive regulatory functions involved in guiding behavior, especially aspects of impulsivity linked to planning ahead and staying on task. In this context, they are contrasted with affective reactivity and refer to the more self-regulating side of behavior.

reasons: The packet only says impulsivity reflects both affective reactivity and cognitive control processes; it does not define control processes as planning ahead, staying on task, or the self-regulating side of behavior.
The contrast with affective reactivity is supported in general, but the definition adds unsupported detail about specific impulsivity facets and their meaning.

The packet does not define “control processes” as “cognitive regulatory functions involved in guiding behavior.” It only states that impulsivity reflects both “affective reactivity and cognitive control processes.”

The definition’s emphasis on “planning ahead” and “staying on task” is not explicitly stated in the packet. While related UPPS facets (e.g., premeditation, perseverance) are mentioned, the packet does not equate these with the general phrase used in the definition.

The definition claims that the term “refers to the more self-regulating side of behavior.” The packet discusses “regulatory facets of impulsivity” but does not explicitly frame cognitive control processes as “the more self-regulating side of behavior.”
